174	export const getPathLength = <P extends LocalPoint | GlobalPoint>(
175	  points: readonly P[],
176	): number => {
177	  let length = 0;
178	  for (let i = 1; i < points.length; i++) {
179	    length += pointDistance(points[i - 1], points[i]);
180	  }

186	 * progress `t` (0..1) along it, interpolating within the containing segment.
187	 * `t` is clamped to [0, 1]; a path with fewer than 2 points returns its only
188	 * point (or the origin if empty).
189	 */
190	export const getPointAtProgress = <P extends LocalPoint | GlobalPoint>(
191	  points: readonly P[],
192	  t: number,
193	): { x: number; y: number } => {
194	  if (points.length === 0) {
195	    return { x: 0, y: 0 };
196	  }
197	  if (points.length === 1) {
198	    return { x: points[0][0], y: points[0][1] };
199	  }
200
201	  const clampedT = Math.min(Math.max(t, 0), 1);
202	  const totalLength = getPathLength(points);
203
204	  if (totalLength === 0) {
205	    return { x: points[0][0], y: points[0][1] };
206	  }
207
208	  const targetLength = clampedT * totalLength;
209	  let traveled = 0;
210
211	  for (let i = 1; i < points.length; i++) {
212	    const segmentLength = pointDistance(points[i - 1], points[i]);
213	    if (traveled + segmentLength >= targetLength || i === points.length - 1) {
214	      const segmentT =
215	        segmentLength === 0 ? 0 : (targetLength - traveled) / segmentLength;
216	      const [x0, y0] = points[i - 1];
217	      const [x1, y1] = points[i];
218	      return {
219	        x: x0 + (x1 - x0) * segmentT,
220	        y: y0 + (y1 - y0) * segmentT,
221	      };
222	    }
223	    traveled += segmentLength;
224	  }
225
226	  const last = points[points.length - 1];
227	  return { x: last[0], y: last[1] };

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-09 01:30:34Z)**_

I made the change. The new tests pass and typecheck is clean.

**Why it happened:** A motion path stores its target as an ID (`targetElementId`) or a group ID (`targetGroupId`). The duplication code copies everything and gives the copies new IDs and group IDs, but it never updated the copied path's target. So the new path still pointed at the original element: the original was tied to two paths, and the duplicate wasn't tied to any.

**The fix** is in `duplicateElements` in `packages/element/src/duplicate.ts`, right after the existing binding and frame fix-ups. For each copied path:

- `targetElementId` is changed to the duplicate's ID, using the `origIdToDuplicateId` map that function already builds.
- `targetGroupId` is changed to the duplicate group's new ID, using the `groupIdMap` it already keeps. I also gave that map a proper type (`Map<GroupId, GroupId>`) so this type-checks.
- If the target wasn't duplicated (you only duplicated the path), the copy keeps pointing at the original element.

Ctrl+D, Alt-drag and copy/paste all go through `duplicateElements`, so they all get this fix. With Alt-drag, the original path stays tied to the original element and the copy to the copy, whichever one ends up being moved.

**Tests:** I added three cases under "motion paths" in `packages/element/tests/duplicate.test.tsx`: a single-element target, a group target, and a path duplicated without its target. Those three plus the existing duplicate and path test files all pass (46 tests), and `yarn test:typecheck` is clean. I didn't run them against the old code to confirm they failed before the fix, and I haven't run the full `yarn test:update`, which `CLAUDE.md` says to do before committing.

**One decision for you:** when only the path is duplicated, the original element ends up on two paths. If you'd rather the copy have no target in that case (it would just sit there doing nothing), change the `?? mutablePath.targetElementId` fallback to `?? null`, and do the same for the group target.

119	        : { elapsed: 0, totalDuration, originalPositions };
120
121	      const t = Math.min(next.elapsed / next.totalDuration, 1);
122
123	      // read the path's geometry live every frame, not once up front: the
124	      // path (and its target with it) can be dragged mid-playback, and the
125	      // target must keep riding the path where it is *now*
126	      const livePath = this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElement(path.id);
127	      const liveGlobalPoints =
128	        livePath && isPathElement(livePath)
129	          ? getPathGlobalSamplePoints(
130	              livePath,
131	              this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap(),
132	            )
133	          : globalPoints;
134	      const liveStartPoint =
135	        livePath && isPathElement(livePath)
136	          ? getPathMotionStartPoint(livePath, liveGlobalPoints)
137	          : startPoint;
138
139	      // eased time → position within the configured start..end section
140	      const progress = motion.start + ease(t) * (motion.end - motion.start);
141	      const { x: dx, y: dy } = getPointAtProgress(liveGlobalPoints, progress);
142	      const totalDeltaX = dx - startPoint.x + alignmentOffset.x;
143	      const totalDeltaY = dy - startPoint.y + alignmentOffset.y;
144	      // how far the path's start has moved since playback began
145	      const pathShiftX = liveStartPoint.x - startPoint.x;
146	      const pathShiftY = liveStartPoint.y - startPoint.y;
147
148	      const liveOriginalPositions = new Map(
149	        [...next.originalPositions].filter(([id]) =>
150	          this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElement(id),
151	        ),
152	      );
153
154	      if (liveOriginalPositions.size === 0) {
155	        return null;
156	      }
157
158	      for (const [id, orig] of liveOriginalPositions) {
159	        const element = this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElement(id);
160	        if (!element) {
161	          continue;
162	        }
163	        this.app.scene.mutateElement(
164	          element,
165	          {
166	            x: orig.x + totalDeltaX,
167	            y: orig.y + totalDeltaY,
168	          },
169	          { informMutation: true, isDragging: true },
170	        );
171	      }
172	      this.app.scheduleNeverCapture();
173
174	      if (t >= 1) {
175	        // back to rest — shifted along with the path if it was moved
176	        // mid-playback, so the two stay together instead of desyncing
177	        for (const [id, orig] of liveOriginalPositions) {
178	          const element = this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElement(id);
179	          if (element) {
180	            this.app.scene.mutateElement(
181	              element,
182	              { x: orig.x + pathShiftX, y: orig.y + pathShiftY },
183	              { informMutation: true, isDragging: false },
184	            );
185	          }
186	        }
187	        this.app.scheduleNeverCapture();
188	        return null;
189	      }
190
191	      return next;
192	    });
193	  }

200	    );

});

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-09 01:49:56Z)**_

I fixed it: holding down on an element now plays its animation, and the element no longer follows your mouse if you move it while holding.

**Why it stuck:** After you hold for `PATH_PLAYBACK_HOLD_MS` (1 second), the animation starts, but the pointer handler keeps treating the press as a normal drag. Once the mouse moved past the drag threshold, the selected element followed it while the animation was also moving it. The move handler already stopped the hold _before_ it fired; nothing stopped the drag _after_ it fired.

**The fix** is in `onPointerMoveFromPointerDownHandler` in `packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx`. Once the hold has started playback (`this.pathPlaybackJustTriggered` is set), the handler now returns early, so the rest of that press is ignored:

```ts
// the hold already started playback: the rest of this press belongs to
// the animation, so don't let it drag the target along with the pointer
if (this.pathPlaybackJustTriggered) {
  return;
}
```

The pointer-up handler already clears that flag, so the next click or drag works as usual. A quick drag before the hold fires still moves the element normally.

**Test:** I added `packages/excalidraw/tests/pathPlaybackHold.test.tsx`. It presses on the element, waits out the hold, then moves and releases the mouse, and checks that the element didn't move. To test only the drag behaviour, it swaps out the animation itself for a stub. It fails without the fix (the element moves 100px) and passes with it. All the path and duplicate tests pass (76), and `yarn test:typecheck` is clean.

**Side effect:** for the rest of that press, the mouse does nothing else either (no box selection, for example). That seems right, since the press is being used for playback.

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-09 02:46:08Z)**_

I made the change: a path duplicated without its target now gets no target, so the original element is no longer pulled along by the copy. All the duplicate and path tests pass (78), `yarn test:typecheck` is clean, and the changed files pass Prettier. (The earlier `yarn prettier` failure came from the `.specstory` file again, not from these files.)

**The change** is in the retargeting loop I added to `duplicateElements` in `packages/element/src/duplicate.ts`. The fallback is now `null` instead of the original target:

```ts
if (mutablePath.targetElementId) {
  mutablePath.targetElementId =
    origIdToDuplicateId.get(mutablePath.targetElementId) ?? null;
}
if (mutablePath.targetGroupId) {
  mutablePath.targetGroupId = groupIdMap.get(mutablePath.targetGroupId) ?? null;
}
```

What happens now when you duplicate a path:

- **Path and its target together:** the copied path drives the copied element, as before.
- **Path on its own:** the copied path has no target and does nothing. The original path and element are unchanged.

A path with no target was already allowed: the code that loads saved drawings accepts it, and the helper that finds a path's targets simply returns nothing. So nothing else needed to change.

**Tests:** in `packages/element/tests/duplicate.test.tsx`, I changed the "path on its own" test to expect no target. I also added a matching test for a path that targets a group.

**Behaviour change to be aware of:** this also covers copy/paste. Copying and pasting just a path gives you a copy with no target, and there's currently no way to give it a target afterwards.
